chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
An eye is not to be assessed on a cloudy day.

key_terms.تُقَاسُ: is to be measured or assessed in a legal context
key_terms.عَيْنٌ: an eye, referring to the bodily organ under legal evaluation
key_terms.غَيْمٍ: cloudiness or overcast conditions that hinder clear assessment
key_terms.يَوْمِ: the day or time in which the assessment takes place

ai.seo_question: Why should an eye not be assessed on a cloudy day in Islamic legal rulings?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the assessment of an eye should not be conducted on a cloudy day. Its significance is that legal evaluation in cases of bodily injury must be carried out under conditions that allow accurate judgment.
